annotations.text:
The board in the product's own voice.

The segmented switcher, the plan board's status header and chips, panel cards, and the usage panel's amount, caption and six-pixel gauge with its 60 and 85 percent marks: every element is one the app already ships, at its shipped values.

Four figures a person understands at a glance: tokens, turns, bounces, and what is waiting on them. Then who spent what, ranked, with the metric switchable. Then runway as the usage gauges.

Every token figure is summed from the agents' own session logs, the files the KPI ledger imports when it is on: 12 Claude sessions under ~/.claude/projects and 2 Codex rollouts under ~/.codex/sessions. tokens.py extracts them into tokens.json; gen_board.py draws the frames. Read at 22:12.

What the numbers say without a sentence: design work wrote 64 percent of today's output tokens, the Orchestrator took 37 percent of all turns and read 54 percent of all context, and 1.2 billion of the 1.22 billion input tokens came back from cache.

The two versions are the same board. The watcher version adds a chip in the header and one card of what it wrote and to whom. Everything on the board is arithmetic a person reads directly; the watcher improves only the two conclusions on the catalogue that are judgments over prose.
Rendered in headless Chrome at 960 and 390 and sized to the content; the frames match the pixels. Every value is lifted from tokens.css, globals.css and the usage panel's stylesheet.
